validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification/StartYear/Owner. See separate spec and duplicate-family flags below for length/diameter nuance and the P3382 relationship.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently, and well beyond GEM-derived material. Three mutually independent sources describe this exact pipeline by name: (1) Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated article 'Шебелинка — Слов'янськ (газопровід)', which states a single 700mm line commissioned 1969 connecting the Shebelynka field (Kharkiv Oblast) to Donbas consumers, and describes the 2015-tendered modernization to 500mm; (2) nashigroshi.org (an independent Ukrainian investigative-journalism outlet, not a wire reprint), 'reconstruction for 96 million' (2015-12-04), on the same modernization tender; (3) tsoua.com (Gas TSO of Ukraine, the official state operator) itself, in its 'Potočni proekty' investment-projects page — captured via Wayback since the live site 403s automated fetches (Cloudflare bot-protection, not evidence the page is gone; verified live via the CDX API) — which gives a highly specific engineering description: built 1969, Du700, unequal-flow cranes, rubber-bitumen insulation now failed (rust, cavities), and a section-by-section (UT-1 through UT-4, km 1.1-55.1) reconstruction plan to Du500. A general web search independently surfaced a fourth line of corroboration: ProZorro/Dozorro Ukrainian public-procurement tender records (e.g. UA-2020-06-10-007174-b) titled 'Реконструкція газопроводу Шебелинка-Слов'янськ (заміна Ду 700 на Ду 500, км 1,1 - 68,0; довжиною 67 км) Краматорського ЛВУМГ, Донецької області' (I could not get a live tender page to pass the verifier — prozorro/dozorro render via JS and return near-empty static HTML — so I have not cited it directly, but its title text corroborates the same project independently of the other three). This is a real, actively-engineered Soviet-era trunk, not a phantom/GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct — a magistral (high-pressure transmission) gas trunk, not a gathering/feeder line; all sources call it 'магістральний газопровід'. StartYear1=1969 confirmed by all three sources. ATTRIBUTION (Owner): Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' 100% is correct per the country-wide rule — confirmed by two independent sources: tsoua.com's own English 'Key Facts' page (Wayback capture, live page 403s) stating GTSOU has been the certified GTS operator since 2020-01-01 and is a subsidiary of JSC Mahistralni Gazoprovody Ukrainy (MGU), itself 100% owned by the Ministry of Finance; and Naftogaz.com's own news article on the completed unbundling, which independently names the same new operator (GTSOU) and the same shareholder (MGU, owned by the Ministry of Finance). No Gazprom stake — consistent with the country rule that a wholly-domestic Ukrainian trunk is never Gazprom-owned.

validity.recommendation: Flag for the redundancy-cluster adjudication pass, cross-reference P3382 ('Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline', len=54.0 dia=500). Do not merge unilaterally — my reading is these are two RELATED but likely physically distinct assets (old vs. new parallel pipe on the same corridor), not a simple double-count, but a human should confirm.
validity.researcher_notes: P3381 and P3382 share the identical pipeline name in the sheet ('Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline') and are clearly the same named corridor, but the tsoua.com official project description resolves WHY the two rows carry different length/diameter rather than being a pure duplicate: TSOUA's own investment-project page describes replacing the original Du700 pipe with a NEW Du500 pipe laid PARALLEL to the existing route ('заміна труби Ду 700 ... на трубу Ду 500 ... шляхом прокладки паралельно існуючий трасі'), in sections UT-1 (km1.1-13.6), UT-2 (km13.6-26.1), UT-3 (km26.1-39.9) and UT-4 (km39.9-55.1) — and explicitly states the plan is to DISMANTLE the old Du700 pipe only AFTER the Du500 section is commissioned ('демонтування існуючого газопроводу ДУ 700 після прийняття в експлуатацію ділянки Ду 500'). Doing the arithmetic on the UT sections: (13.6-1.1)+(26.1-13.6)+(39.9-26.1)+(55.1-39.9) = 12.5+12.5+13.8+15.2 = 54.0 km — an EXACT match to P3382's LengthKnown=54.0 and DiameterUnits=500mm. This is too precise to be coincidence: P3382 is almost certainly GEM's entry for the new/parallel Du500 pipe covering exactly the UT-1–UT-4 corridor (km1.1–55.1), while P3381 (this row, 70km, Du700, built 1969) is the ORIGINAL full-corridor pipe. So the pair likely represents two related-but-distinct physical assets mid-transition (old full-length line + new partial-length parallel replacement under construction), analogous to the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pattern rather than a straightforward double-count — BUT there is real double-count risk if/once the Du500 section is fully commissioned and the Du700 section over that same 54km stretch is formally dismantled per TSOUA's own stated plan: at that point P3381's full 70km would overlap the now-decommissioned middle of the corridor with P3382's 54km of live pipe, and P3381's Status/Length would need updating to reflect only the still-operating Du700 remainder (roughly km0-1.1 and km55.1-68.6/70, i.e. ~14-16km) rather than the full 70km. I could not verify whether the Du700 dismantling has actually happened as of 2026 (see spec/status caveat below) — leaving that determination, and the merge/no-merge call, to the cluster adjudication pass.

validity.recommendation: No value change proposed. Flag for future monitoring: TSOUA's own 2021 plan calls for eventual full dismantling of the Du700 pipe once its Du500 parallel replacement is commissioned corridor-wide; if that has since occurred, both LengthKnown (currently 70.00km, full corridor) and Diameter (700mm) would need revisiting to reflect only the surviving Du700 remainder. No dated evidence found that the dismantling has actually happened, so I am not proposing a change now.
validity.researcher_notes: Length: sources cluster tightly around 67-68.6km for the corridor rather than exactly matching the sheet's 70.00km — Ukrainian Wikipedia and the ProZorro tender title both give '67 km' (km1.1 to km68.0), and TSOUA's own project text extends the reconstruction scope to km68.6 (i.e. ~67.5km from km1.1, or ~68.6km including the initial approach). A ~2-3km / ~3-4% gap from the sheet's 70.00km is not large enough on its own to call material (well under the >10% material-conflict threshold used elsewhere in this project), and is plausibly just a difference in where the corridor's km-0 reference point sits (technical km-markers along the pipe vs. straight-line/as-built distance) — so I am treating 70.00km as reasonably corroborated rather than wrong, with this noted as a minor caveat. Diameter: 700mm is solidly confirmed AS-BUILT (1969) by all three existence sources, but is NOT necessarily the CURRENT diameter along the whole corridor — TSOUA's 2021 document already describes km1.1-26.1 (UT-1/UT-2) as completed replacement to Du500, with UT-3/UT-4 (km26.1-55.1) 'ongoing', and further reconstruction of km55.1-68.6 to Du500 as still needed at that time, culminating in planned dismantling of the Du700 pipe. That means by the time of my research (2026), the physical pipe recorded as 700mm here may already be partially or wholly superseded/removed over some or all of its length — but I found no 2023-2025 source confirming project completion or dismantling one way or the other (Ukrainian search turned up no post-2021 status update specific to this project; the front-line proximity of Sloviansk since 2022 makes verification harder and also raises independent doubt about whether reconstruction work continued). Recommend leaving Diameter=700mm as-is (still the best-supported, most recently confirmed figure) but flagging this row for a repeat check once the war situation allows better visibility.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources treat the pipeline as a live, in-service transmission asset undergoing active maintenance/reconstruction (the whole point of a reconstruction project is to keep an operating line safe) rather than a retired one. I found no dated evidence that the Du700 pipe has been decommissioned since; per the country-scope rule I am not inferring a status change from the end of Russian transit (irrelevant to this domestic Donbas-supply line) or from the war generally (no line-specific damage/closure report found) — tier medium rather than high because neither source is a direct 2026 'still operating today' statement, just the most recent dated evidence available plus the absence of any contrary report.
Both sources describe this as a 'газопровід' (gas pipeline) carrying natural gas from the Shebelynka gas field; Fuel=Gas is correct.

Ukrainian Wikipedia and TSOUA's own (Wayback-captured) project page independently state the pipeline was built/commissioned in 1969; TSOUA's text is highly specific ('побудований у 1969 р.', built in 1969) matching GEM's StartYear1=1969 exactly.

700mm (Du700) as-built diameter is confirmed by both sources. See the spec caveat in validity[]: this is the historically correct and best-currently-supported figure, but TSOUA's own document describes an active, partially-completed plan to replace it with Du500 along most of the corridor and eventually dismantle the Du700 pipe — no evidence found that this has been completed as of 2026, so 700mm stands.

Neither source states exactly '70.00 km' — Ukrainian Wikipedia and a ProZorro tender title both say '67 km' (corridor km1.1 to km68.0), and TSOUA's own project text extends the reconstruction scope to km68.6. 70.00km is close to, but not an exact match for, this ~67-68.6km cluster (a ~3-4% gap, i.e. below the >10% material-conflict threshold). Tier medium (not high) to reflect that the sources corroborate the pipeline's approximate length and corridor extent rather than exactly the stated 70.00km figure; see the spec caveat in validity[] for the full reasoning. Not proposing a value change.

Endpoints confirmed by both sources (Shebelynka field in Kharkiv Oblast; Slovyansk in Donbas). TSOUA's official text explicitly names both oblasts together — 'donets'koi oblasti i skhodu Kharkivs'koi oblasti' (Donetsk oblast and eastern Kharkiv oblast) — as the consumers this line supplies, corroborating StartState/Province=Kharkiv Oblast and EndState/Province=Donetsk Oblast (both currently blank on the sheet); Ukrainian Wikipedia independently states the Shebelynka field sits in Kharkiv Oblast.

Independently, Naftogaz.com's own news article on the completed unbundling names the same operator (GTSOU) and the same shareholder/ownership chain (MGU, Ministry of Finance) — a second, organizationally distinct publisher (Naftogaz, the former parent, reporting on its own separation) confirming the same structure. summary: P3381 (Shebelinka-Slovyansk, Du700, 1969) exists, is correctly classified/attributed (GTSOU/MGU, not Gazprom) and its core specs (1969, 700mm, Shebelinka/Kharkiv Oblast to Slovyansk/Donetsk Oblast) are confirmed by 3 independent sources (Ukrainian Wikipedia, nashigroshi.org, TSOUA's own archived project page); flagged a likely DUPLICATE-FAMILY relationship with P3382 (54km/500mm exactly matches the UT-1-UT-4 replacement segment of this same corridor per TSOUA's own reconstruction plan, which calls for eventually dismantling this row's Du700 pipe) and a minor SPEC caveat (independent sources give 67-68.6km vs. the sheet's 70.00km — close but not exact, no change proposed). No UNRESOLVED units.
